channel.title: OT/ICS Threat Intel - All Critical Infrastructure
channel.description: Curated OT/ICS advisories, incidents and threat intelligence. Editorial by Mike Holcomb in partnership with UtilSec.

item.title: [Critical] Russia-aligned hackers are manipulating exposed industrial controls across NATO countries, Bloomberg reports
item.description: Bloomberg’s 27 October investigation describes a loose network of pro-Russian hacktivist crews, chiefly CARR and Z-Pentest, tampering with exposed industrial controls across NATO countries since late 2024. Documented cases include a Danish water-pump controller set to zero pressure and then surged, bursting pipes and cutting water to about 450 homes (password “1234”); a Los Angeles-area meatpacker whose refrigeration was shut off, causing an ammonia leak; and Spanish crematorium, winery and transformer-factory incidents. Attribution of individual cases is mostly unconfirmed and CISA says these groups exaggerate, yet US charges and sanctions treat CARR as GRU-directed. The common thread is internet-exposed controllers with weak passwords, not sophisticated malware, so basic exposure and password hygiene blocks most of it. - Bloomberg News via Bloomberg Law (27 Oct 2026; partly paywalled); Meduza summary (28 Oct 2026); Tech Times (29 Oct 2026) - Published 27 Oct 2026; incidents span late 2024 to summer 2026

item.title: [High] The Pentagon is treating August freezer failures at US military base stores as a suspected cyberattack, Reuters reports
item.category: Incident — Suspected cyberattack on refrigeration at US military commissaries; reported 29 Oct
item.description: Reuters reported on 29 October, citing four unnamed officials, that investigators suspect hackers caused refrigerators and freezers at no fewer than six US military commissaries to switch to defrost mode in late August, spoiling food. A Cyber Command unit and Army criminal investigators are involved and have spoken with French police about the October supermarket attack. The cause, the entry route and any responsible party are not established, and Reuters could not confirm that Danfoss or any other controller brand was used. The Pentagon has acknowledged only that the refrigeration problems occurred. - Reuters (29 Oct 2026), via The Business Standard and The Next Web - Published 29 Oct 2026; incidents occurred in late August 2026 — investigation ongoing

item.title: [Critical] French supermarket refrigeration attack: about 700 stores hit, and Forescout counts nearly 13,000 exposed refrigeration controllers worldwide
item.category: Incident — Attack on refrigeration controllers at about 700 French supermarkets, 11–13 Oct; Forescout exposure data 22 Oct
item.description: Attackers forced web-managed refrigeration controllers into continuous defrost at French supermarkets on the nights of 11–13 October; France’s finance minister put the toll at about 700 stores, and the Paris prosecutor, working with ANSSI, says fires also resulted. CERT-FR names Danfoss AK-SC and AK-SM plus Copeland and Dixell XWEB controllers and judged on 16 October that the campaigns are probably still under way. On 22 October Forescout reported 12,976 internet-exposed refrigeration management services in 99 countries; most affected units are end-of-life. No actor, CVE or entry route has been named, and no new attack nights have been reported since 13 October. - CERT-FR alert CERTFR-2026-ALE-012 (v3 16 Oct); Forescout Vedere Labs (22 Oct 2026); The Record (20 Oct 2026) - Attacks on 11–13 Oct 2026, none reported since; updated 22 Oct 2026 with Forescout exposure data — investigation ongoing

item.title: [Medium] Ukraine’s CERT-UA warns that attackers are taking over Dahua surveillance cameras and recorders
item.category: Incident — CERT-UA warns that internet-connected Dahua cameras and recorders are being compromised, apparently through the Easy4IP cloud feature and 2021 authentication-bypass flaws; actor, victims and device counts undisclosed
item.description: In a warning issued late in the week before The Record reported it on 26 October, CERT-UA said attackers had compromised internet-connected Dahua cameras and network video recorders, changed their settings and created unauthorized user accounts. They appear to abuse Dahua’s Easy4IP cloud remote-access feature: serial numbers follow predictable patterns, so cloud-connected units can be found by guessing and then opened with weak or default passwords or through outdated firmware; CERT-UA flagged the 2021 authentication bypasses CVE-2021-33044 and CVE-2021-33045. The agency did not say how many devices were hit, when, by whom, or which organizations own them. Cameras and recorders are common on plant perimeters, substations, pumping stations and terminals, and they often sit on the same networks as operations gear, so an exposed unit is both a surveillance risk and a possible foothold (editorial assessment). - Recorded Future News / The Record (26 Oct 2026), citing CERT-UA and Hunt.io; CISA KEV catalog - CERT-UA warning issued in the week before 26 Oct 2026 (exact date not given); reported 26 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] CISA, the FBI and partners warn that SafePay ransomware has hit at least 600 organizations since August 2024
item.category: Advisory — joint advisory AA26-293A from CISA, the FBI, the US Secret Service and German and UK partners on SafePay ransomware, which the agencies say has hit at least 600 organizations across multiple critical-infrastructure sectors
item.description: Advisory AA26-293A, issued on 20 October by CISA, the FBI and the US Secret Service with Germany’s LKA Rheinland-Pfalz, the UK National Crime Agency and the North West Regional Organised Crime Unit, says SafePay has hit at least 600 organizations from multiple critical-infrastructure sectors in North America, South America, Europe and Australia. Entry is usually through exposed or brute-forced credentials, phished accounts, VPN logins from Mullvad addresses and automated exploitation of edge-device flaws; the group then steals data, deletes shadow copies, resets network-attached storage that holds backups and moves with tools such as WinRM, PsExec and RDP. The advisory carries indicators and ATT&CK mappings for activity from November 2024 to August 2026. It names no victims, and reporting on it describes no OT, energy or water impact, so the OT risk here is the usual one: a ransomware crew reaching the IT network that plant systems depend on. - CISA advisory AA26-293A (20 Oct 2026), as reported by BleepingComputer and Cybersecurity Dive - Published 20 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Ransomware crews are now using the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass to get past MFA and into networks, including utilities, energy and manufacturers
item.category: Incident report — Unit 42 update: ransomware crews (Qilin, Inc and Settra) exploiting the PAN-OS GlobalProtect authentication bypass CVE-2026-0257, in CISA KEV since 29 May 2026
item.description: Palo Alto Networks’ Unit 42 updated its brief on 19–20 October to report that ransomware operators are exploiting CVE-2026-0257, an authentication bypass in the PAN-OS GlobalProtect portal and gateway, to start VPN sessions without valid credentials and bypass MFA. Unit 42 ties the activity to Spikey Scorpius (Qilin) and Tarnished Scorpius (Inc), and public reporting also names Settra. Exploitation was first seen in June, after a proof of concept appeared on 29 May; the flaw was fixed in May and added to CISA’s KEV catalog on 29 May. Targeted sectors include utilities and energy, manufacturing, and transportation and logistics. After entry the crews use remote-management tools, move over RDP and SMB, and in one case pivoted to vCenter, disabled security controls on ESXi hosts and dumped credentials from a domain controller’s virtual disk. No OT impact is reported. - Unit 42 (Palo Alto Networks) brief, updated 19–20 Oct 2026; Help Net Security; CISA KEV catalog - Ransomware use reported 19–20 Oct 2026; in KEV since 29 May 2026 — re-warned on new ransomware activity

item.title: [Medium] Albert Heijn restarts home deliveries after the Ahold Delhaize cyberattack; the group confirms malicious activity, and stores stayed open
item.category: Incident — cyberattack on a major grocery group’s IT and online services that disrupted logistics; not a confirmed OT compromise (Food & Ag-adjacent)
item.description: Albert Heijn restarted grocery home deliveries on 23 October at about a third of normal capacity, nearly two weeks after Ahold Delhaize took systems offline on 12 October across most of its brands in Europe and the US; it expected to deliver all orders again from 28 October (not yet confirmed), and Dutch police are investigating the attack as a criminal case (NL Times). In its latest statement, on 19 October, the group said outside experts had confirmed “malicious actions of others”, that it had notified the Dutch NCSC and filed a police report, and that it had no evidence so far that sensitive data was taken; stores stayed open throughout. Ahold Delhaize USA’s banner websites and apps came back online on 20 October (Grocery Dive). The group has issued no cyber update since 19 October; its third-quarter results are due on 4 November. Albert Heijn said its distribution centres had to be restarted on 13–14 October (as reported by NL Times). No attacker or ransomware claim is known. This was an IT-side attack that disrupted logistics, not a confirmed OT compromise, and the Dutch NCSC saw no link to the French refrigeration attack. - Ahold Delhaize statements (12, 13–14 and 19 Oct 2026); NL Times (15 and 23 Oct 2026); Grocery Dive (20 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (20 Oct 2026) - Systems offline 12 Oct 2026; malicious activity confirmed 19 Oct 2026; Albert Heijn deliveries restarted at about a third of capacity and police investigation reported 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [Info] The “Blue Initiative” maritime coalition launches a public repository of IT and OT vulnerabilities for shipping
item.category: Resource — public database of maritime-relevant IT/OT vulnerabilities (the Maritime Vulnerabilities Repository), launched by the Blue Initiative coalition by 26 October 2026
item.description: Cydome, Rakuten Maritime, Bureau Veritas, ClassNK and MTS-ISAC, working together as the Blue Initiative, have launched the Maritime Vulnerabilities Repository, a public database limited to IT and OT vulnerabilities relevant to the maritime sector (Infosecurity Magazine, 26 October). Researchers from Cydome and the other partners review proposed entries before publication, and entries are published only once a patch is available. Users can filter by equipment or vendor, read analyst notes and subscribe to alerts. SecurityWeek, which describes the database as free and covering ship and port systems, reports nearly 30,000 entries, more than 580 of them known to be exploited and only 37 tied to maritime-specific products; those figures appear only in its report and could not be verified. It is a resource launch, not a new threat report, but it gives vessel and terminal operators a maritime-specific way to prioritize patching (editorial assessment). - Infosecurity Magazine (26 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek (27 Oct 2026) - Launched by 26 Oct 2026

item.title: [Medium] AI-agent ransomware toolkit “Phantom” used edge and remote-access flaws, with industrial and manufacturing firms the largest group of targets
item.category: Threat Intel — SOCRadar analysis of AI-assisted ransomware intrusions; industrial and manufacturing firms are the largest group (about 16%) of 62 named targets
item.description: SOCRadar researchers (report published 20 October, updated 23 October, and covered by The Hacker News on 23 October) found an exposed server showing affiliates of the INC and The Gentlemen ransomware groups running intrusions through an AI-agent framework called Phantom, with a human operator writing prompts and reviewing each step. According to the operator’s own records, entry came through internet-facing systems such as FortiClient EMS, SimpleHelp, cPanel and VPN gateways, and one reused password opened VPN, backup, remote-management and security platforms. SOCRadar lists 62 named target organisations, 36 of them in the US, with industrial and manufacturing firms the largest group (about 16%, roughly ten organisations); four appeared on leak sites. The activity is IT-side data theft and extortion; the report describes no access to controllers or SCADA, but the same edge entry points and reused credentials are what an attacker needs to reach OT-adjacent networks. - SOCRadar (20 Oct 2026, updated 23 Oct 2026); The Hacker News (23 Oct 2026) - SOCRadar report 20 Oct 2026, updated 23 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] EPICS Base control-system toolkit: four flaws, one rated critical, found by an AI agent in under four hours
item.category: Advisory — CISA ICSA-26-300-01 (27 Oct): four EPICS Base vulnerabilities, fixed in 7.0.11; no exploitation reported
item.description: CISA published an advisory on 27 October for EPICS Base through 7.0.10, the open-source control-system toolkit used at scientific facilities and some industrial sites. The Register reports that Causal Security’s autonomous agent “Cipher” found and validated all four flaws in 3 hours 49 minutes with one human instruction; the worst, an integer overflow leading to a heap write and possible code execution, is rated CVSS v3.1 9.8. The other three are out-of-bounds writes and reads, and a type confusion, that can crash services. Exploitation needs network reach to the vulnerable services, so flat or poorly segmented control networks carry the risk. The maintainers warn that older Channel Access clients may not work with 7.0.11. - CISA ICSA-26-300-01 (27 Oct 2026); The Register (27 Oct 2026), citing Causal Security - CISA advisory 27 Oct 2026; The Register report 27 Oct 2026

item.title: [Critical] PHP2Shell is in CISA KEV and Palo Alto reports attacks on exposed PAN-OS management interfaces; Siemens, Schneider and ABB list affected OT products, and Schneider now has a Control Engineering fix
item.category: Advisory — PHP2Shell (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2 per the PHP Group): both in CISA KEV since 26 Oct; Palo Alto reports exploitation of internet-exposed PAN-OS management interfaces; Siemens, Schneider and ABB list affected OT products; no OT victim named
item.description: PHP2Shell is a pair of unauthenticated remote-code-execution flaws in PHP (CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619, CVSS v4.0 9.2 per the PHP Group) fixed on 21 October in PHP 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. Exploitation attempts began on 17 October, and over 24–25 October researchers at Perplexity, backed by Expel’s Marcus Hutchins, confirmed working remote code execution against a honeypot. CISA, which had published a SIGMA detection rule on 23 October, added both flaws to its KEV catalog on 26 October with a 29 October federal deadline, without describing the activity. Palo Alto Networks’ advisory, raised to Critical on 27 October and updated on 28 October, reports active exploitation targeting PAN-OS management interfaces exposed to the internet on PA-Series, VM-Series and Panorama (web UI and XML API; GlobalProtect is not affected); it names no victims, and hotfixes are rolling out 21–30 October. That reaches OT directly: Siemens’ SSA-566512 lists RUGGEDCOM APE1808 units running PAN-OS as affected, with remediation through Siemens customer support plus Palo Alto’s workarounds. Schneider’s bulletin SESB-2026-295-01, revised to v2.0.0 on 26 October, says remediation is now available for EcoStruxure Control Engineering (applied automatically when the VM can reach the debian.org and sury.org repositories; otherwise request a patch from Schneider support); Security Expert is fixed in 1.48.4.0 and LINEoptimize is handled through ProLeiT support. ABB lists APROL R 4.4-65 and earlier, with patches planned for 26 and 29 October, and ABB MES installations that use DokuWiki (update PHP or shut DokuWiki down). On 29 October The Register reported that Israeli startup Dream, with Unit 42 verifying the attacker tooling, found suspected China-linked intruders who chained the PHP2Shell flaws with a Linux kernel bug to gain root on 25 PAN-OS 12.1/12.2 firewall servers across the US, Japan, Taiwan and South Korea before moving into Active Directory (attribution suspected, not confirmed; no OT impact described). Rockwell (SD1802, 23 October) has confirmed no affected products while its review continues, and Siemens lists 31 software products and 20 Smart Infrastructure products as not affected, with its evaluation ongoing. No victim organisation has been named and no compromise of an OT product has been reported. Sophos and Unit 42 withdrew earlier reports of successful exploitation, including Unit 42’s link to a European government agency compromise, and CYFIRMA’s tie between a scanning campaign and North Korea is a single-vendor assessment. Software that bundles PHP is easy to miss in IT patch sweeps (editorial assessment), so ask OT vendors directly. - Palo Alto Networks advisory for CVE-2026-109618 (raised to Critical 27 Oct, updated 28 Oct 2026); CISA KEV catalog (27 Oct 2026 release); Schneider Electric SESB-2026-295-01 v2.0.0 (26 Oct 2026); Siemens SSA-566512 (23 Oct 2026), SSA-566435 and SSA-166980; ABB SA26P015 and 4HZK000017 (23 Oct 2026); Rockwell SD1802 (23 Oct 2026); BleepingComputer (26 Oct 2026, honeypot RCE); The Hacker News (25 Oct 2026, CYFIRMA claim) - Exploitation attempts since 17 Oct 2026; PHP fixes 21 Oct 2026; honeypot RCE 24–25 Oct 2026; Schneider Control Engineering remediation 26 Oct 2026; CISA KEV addition 26 Oct 2026 (federal deadline 29 Oct); Palo Alto advisory raised to Critical 27 Oct and updated 28 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] October ICS fixes: critical ICONICS GENESIS64 flaws and a WAGO controller bug join Siemens, Rockwell and ABB, and some Siemens flaws still have no fix
item.category: Advisory — October ICS advisories: CISA’s 22 Oct republication of Siemens’ 13 Oct advisories, its 20 Oct batch (WAGO, Moxa), Mitsubishi Electric ICONICS GENESIS64 (15 Oct; republished by CISA as ICSA-26-300-02 on 27 Oct), Rockwell 1732E ArmorBlock and ABB dynovaPRO; no exploitation reported
item.description: On 22 October CISA republished Siemens’ 13 October advisories (ICSA-26-295-02 to -18): fixes are still pending for the S7 PLC web server, the S7-1500 MFP Linux subsystems and WinCC V7.5, and none is planned for APOGEE MBC/MEC. CISA’s 20 October batch covered WAGO controller firmware (CVE-2026-80466, CVSS v3.1 8.8: a low-privileged user can inject commands that run as root; fixed in 4.10.0/FW32) and Moxa’s AIG-302 edge gateway (hard-coded key CVE-2026-109813, v3.1 8.1 / v4.0 8.6; fixed in 1.4.1). Mitsubishi Electric’s 15 October advisory fixes an authentication bypass (CVE-2026-16436, CVSS v3.1 8.1) and over-permissive DCOM defaults (CVE-2026-16438, v3.1 9.1) across ICONICS GENESIS64, GENESIS, Hyper Historian and related products; MC Works64, GENESIS32 and BizViz get no fix, and Mitsubishi advises replacing them. CISA republished the advisory on 27 October as ICSA-26-300-02. Earlier in the month Rockwell fixed a critical 1732E ArmorBlock admin-takeover flaw and ABB a dynovaPRO password-reset flaw. None is reported exploited. - CISA ICS advisories ICSA-26-293-02 and -03 (20 Oct 2026) and ICSA-26-295-02 to -18 (22 Oct 2026); Mitsubishi Electric advisory 2026-006 (15 Oct 2026), republished by CISA as ICSA-26-300-02 (27 Oct 2026); SecurityWeek ICS Patch Tuesday (14 Oct 2026), summarizing Siemens ProductCERT, Rockwell, Schneider Electric and ABB releases - Siemens, Rockwell and ABB releases 13–14 Oct 2026; Mitsubishi Electric 15 Oct 2026; CISA batches 20, 22 and 27 Oct 2026

item.title: [High] Siemens confirms a Software Center flaw is being exploited to deliver malware, and CISA adds it to the KEV catalog
item.category: Advisory — Siemens Software Center uncontrolled search-path (DLL side-loading) flaw CVE-2026-110936 (CVSS v3.1 6.7 / v4.0 8.4) exploited in the “Romulus” ClickFix campaign; in CISA KEV since 20 Oct 2026
item.description: Siemens first published CVE-2026-110936 on 15 October and on 19 October confirmed it is being exploited. Software Center, the tool engineers use to install and update Siemens software, did not restrict where it searches for helper DLLs, so attackers paired a genuine, validly signed copy with their own malicious libraries in an installer package. Siemens ties the activity to the “Romulus” multi-platform ClickFix campaign, which tricks users into running pasted commands, and names no final malware family. It says no Siemens system, product or update channel was breached, to its knowledge. Version 4.0.9.8 fixes the flaw, and installed copies update on next start. CISA added the flaw to KEV on 20 October with a 3 November deadline and has republished Siemens’ advisory as ICSA-26-295-03. Exploitation needs local access and a user who runs the lure, so engineering workstations running Siemens tooling are the exposure. - Siemens ProductCERT advisory SSA-580366 and blog (19 Oct 2026); CISA KEV catalog and advisory ICSA-26-295-03; SecurityWeek (19 Oct 2026) - Disclosed 15 Oct 2026; exploitation confirmed 19 Oct 2026; added to KEV 20 Oct 2026 (federal deadline 3 Nov 2026)

item.title: [Info] Centrii warns low-impact grid sites to prove NERC CIP-003-9 vendor remote access controls before auditors ask
item.category: Regulation — NERC CIP-003-9 vendor remote access controls for low-impact BES systems (in effect since 1 April 2026); audit-readiness warning; no CVE
item.description: In a 26 October analysis, compliance firm Centrii says CIP-003-9, in effect since 1 April 2026, now requires owners of low-impact bulk electric system assets that allow vendor remote access to have three processes: identify vendor remote access, disable it, and detect known or suspected malicious communications tied to it. The standard does not define “vendor”, and ReliabilityFirst expects auditors to read it broadly, including staff augmentation. Centrii flags records as the weak spot: evidence must be kept for three calendar years, audits of low-impact requirements can reach back six, and the proof is often scattered across email, equipment-maker support portals and contractor systems. The owner stays accountable even when operations are outsourced. Centrii recommends one named person to approve each vendor access path, one to disable it and one place for records. This is a vendor’s compliance commentary, not a regulator statement. - Centrii analysis, as reported by Industrial Cyber - Published 26 Oct 2026; CIP-003-9 in effect since 1 Apr 2026
